newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grundig sees 1997 loss, 1998 oper profit.
newsitem.headline: Grundig sees 1997 loss, 1998 oper profit.

text.p: Loss-making German consumer electronics maker Grundig AG expects to post another loss this year, but hopes to show an operating profit in early 1998, chairman Pieter van der Wal told a news conference.

The company will show an improved result but still be in the red this year, van der Wal said. It will be able to cover the loss from reserves. Sales will be about three billion marks ($1.9 billion). Earlier, he had estimated the 1996 loss at 250 million marks, narrowing from a record 600 million mark loss the year before.

Grundig is actively seeking new partners following the surprise pullout earlier this week of Philips N.V., which opens opportunities as well as risks, van der Wal said. Philips retains its 32 percent stake, but will scale back its role to that of a passive minority stakeholder.
Grundig may operate on its own for awhile, but in the long term it will not last without a strong partner, van der Wal said.
Grundig's search includes companies outside the audio-video sphere, and he expects to find a partner by the end of this year, he said.
Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber said late on Wednesday the state would not take a stake in Grundig.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-2609750 ($ = 1.577 German Marks)
